Article Title: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warns AI is making hacking ‘dangerously’ easy, explains how
Article Text:
Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks

Nikesh Arora: One hacker can now do the work of 19 using AI agents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora has issued a stark warning that artificial intelligence (AI) is making cyberattacks significantly easier to execute, pointing out that AI tools are uncovering decades of human coding flaws at an alarming pace, and hackers are reaping the rewards. Speaking at an Economic Times event, Arora noted that Anthropic’s Mythos is rapidly exposing 50 years' worth of human software mistakes in a remarkably short timeframe, handing a major advantage to cybercriminals. He also highlighted that the flaws that were deemed ‘uncrackable’ by humans, are being exploited by criminals with the new technology.“We've written bad code for 50 years. And unfortunately, AI is busy finding out all those vulnerabilities in a very short span of time. And it's ended up being a bit of a boon for bad actors whose entire reason to exist is that they look for ways to get into companies,” Arora said.To illustrate just how much the threat landscape has shifted with AI, Arora pointed to a recent real-world incident showing how the technology multiplies a single attacker's reach. He said that in one recent case, a single hacker used an AI model on the dark web to attack 19 companies at the exact same time.According to Arora, an operation that previously would have required 19 people working over many days was carried out by one individual deploying an AI agent across all 19 targets.“So I think that is just the beginning. It is unfortunately most likely to come to a theater near you,” he noted, adding that beyond speeding up attacks, AI is breaking through security flaws that human experts once thought were safe from exploitation.“There have been vulnerabilities which were deemed to not be crackable by humans. AI has been able to crack those,” he explained, adding that the industry has entered a new era where organisations must go back and repair historical security flaws they created over the decades.“There have been vulnerabilities which were deemed to not be crackable by humans. AI has been able to crack those. So I think we're in a bit of a new era where we're going to have to go fix all these problems that we've created historically and that is going to be a journey. It's going to take us 12 to 18 months and I think it's going to be a bit of an open season for bad actors,” he said.
Article Summary: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warns that artificial intelligence is making cyberattacks significantly easier to execute. He said that Anthropic’s Mythos is rapidly exposing 50 years' worth of human software mistakes in a remarkably short timeframe, handing a major advantage to cybercriminals.

Article Title: US may ban China-made cars as lawmakers reach deal with auto industry: What it could mean for Tesla, Ford and others
Article Text:
Representative image

Mercedes and Volvo could be exempt from the ban

Batteries excluded from the proposed restrictions

Chinese cars already face 100% tariffs in the US

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US Congress is moving closer to passing a bipartisan bill that would ban the sale of cars linked to China and Russia, with lawmakers aiming to pass the legislation in December. The development comes after key automakers raised concerns over some provisions of the bill, according to a report by Politico. The Connected Vehicle Security Act, introduced by Republican Senator Bernie Moreno and Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, seeks to block the sale of vehicles made using components from countries considered foreign adversaries, including China and Russia.The lawmakers are working to pass the bill through a voice vote in the Senate and fast-track it in the House of Representatives.The original version of the bill proposed banning vehicles made by companies with more than 15% Chinese ownership. This raised concerns for Mercedes-Benz and Volvo, given their Chinese shareholding. Chinese investors own nearly 80% of Volvo and 20% of Mercedes.However, lawmakers have agreed to revise the ownership rules. Under the revised proposal, companies with silent shareholders would get more flexibility, meaning neither Mercedes nor Volvo would be blocked from selling cars in the US, according to people familiar with the discussions cited by POLITICO.A spokesperson for the Alliance for Automotive Innovation, which represents major carmakers including Mercedes, Volvo, General Motors, Ford and Stellantis, told POLITICO the organisation is “very supportive” of the bill.Mercedes-Benz said it “applauds the constructive discussions with key U.S. lawmakers including Senator Moreno, Senator Slotkin and [Senate Commerce Committee] Chairman [Ted] Cruz (R-Texas).”Lawmakers have also decided not to include batteries in the list of components covered by the legislation. Instead, the proposed restrictions will focus on battery management systems. The decision could leave Ford's partnership with Chinese battery maker CATL unaffected. The partnership involves licensing CATL's battery technology.The bill will also include a sunset provision, meaning the proposed ban will not remain in place indefinitely. This follows concerns that restricting affordable Chinese electric vehicles could slow efforts to reduce carbon emissions.Chinese vehicles already face 100% import tariffs in the US, along with restrictions imposed by the Commerce Department on certain vehicle components. However, supporters of the new bill want to make these restrictions part of federal law. This would provide greater certainty to domestic automakers when making long-term decisions about sourcing components.The proposed legislation could also add to tensions between Washington and Beijing as both countries continue discussions over extending their trade truce, which is due to expire on January 10.Describing the progress of the negotiations, one person familiar with the discussions told POLITICO: “This is ‘a freight train that’s moving,’” said one of the people familiar with the discussions. “Slotkin and Moreno are putting people in rooms to make this stuff happen.”
Article Summary: The Connected Vehicle Security Act seeks to block the sale of vehicles made using components from countries considered foreign adversaries. Lawmakers are working to pass the bill through a voice vote in the Senate and fast-track it in the House of Representatives. The original version of the bill proposed banning vehicles made by companies with more than 15% Chinese ownership.

Article Title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan bets on 141-member ‘dream team’, says ‘my number one priority…’

“Now I’m tripling down. This is my number one priority, to make sure that we have the best CPU coming up.”

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan wants to bring back ‘tick-tock’

“This team is only two months old; they already have 141 people and really good CPU architects,”

“tick-tock”

“So I want to go back to the tick-tock, internal team and external team, and then we can continue that way.”

Lip-Bu Tan on catching up with AMD’s Lisa Su

“I only have 18 months, so give me a little bit of time to catch up with it,”

Intel has assembled a 141-person CPU design team. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bets the group can speed up processor development and help the chipmaker regain ground lost to AMD. The team was just two months old when Tan disclosed its size during a last week interview with investor Gavin Baker at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin.Tan said.The new group will work on future designs while Intel’s existing engineers develop its next generation of server processors.Tan said. He wants the new group to work at startup speed and give Intel a second team that can develop processor architectures on a separate schedule.Tan described the plan as a return to Intel’s formerrhythm, adapted to alternate between internal and external architecture teams.he said.Intel’s existing team is working on Diamond Rapids and Coral Rapids, two upcoming lines of Xeon server processors.Tan pointed to simultaneous multithreading, which allows a processor core to handle multiple threads, as one way to improve performance against AMD. Intel has said it is focusing resources on the 16-channel version of Diamond Rapids and looking for ways to accelerate Coral Rapids. Intel earnings remarks.Tan praised AMD CEO Lisa Su’s execution and said she had a 12- to 13-year head start on her turnaround.he said. He also pointed to a practical advantage for AMD. The rival chipmaker can shift supply from PCs to data centers more readily, while differences between Intel’s PC and server chip designs have made that harder for Intel. TomorrowX Summit interviewTan expects the server CPU market to grow from about $40 billion to around $200 billion within five years. He sees AI agents driving some of that growth because CPUs can coordinate work across applications and systems. To capture that demand, Intel will need to deliver chips that compete with AMD’s and manufacture enough of them to meet data center customers’ orders.
Article Summary: Intel has assembled a 141-person CPU design team. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bets the group can speed up processor development. New group will work on future designs while existing engineers develop next generation of server processors. Tan expects the server CPU market to grow from about $40 billion to around $200 billion in five years.

Article Title: Weeks after Canada union win, Amazon workers protest in Germany, the US, Poland and Brazil from Black Friday to Cyber Monday; union leader says the question now is not whether Amazon workers can win,
Article Text:
Amazon workers and supporters are striking and protesting in more than 20 countries from Black Friday to Cyber Monday under the Make Amazon Pay campaign. (AP Photo/Jenny Kane)

Protests stretch from German warehouses to Poland, the US and Brazil

Amazon's first North American union contract came through arbitration

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your view on the role of unions in modern workplaces? They are vital for worker protection They complicate negotiations They have lost relevance I am unsure about their role 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Amazon workers and their supporters are striking and protesting in more than 20 countries this weekend, from Black Friday on November 27 to Cyber Monday on November 30. It comes two weeks after warehouse workers in British Columbia, Canada, won the first binding union contract for Amazon employees anywhere in North America.The global days of action run under the Make Amazon Pay banner, convened by UNI Global Union and the Progressive International. Now in its seventh year, the campaign has one central demand: Amazon must respect workers' right to organise and negotiate with their unions in every country where it operates."The question is no longer whether Amazon workers can win, but where they win next," said Christy Hoffman, General Secretary of UNI Global Union.In Germany, the union ver.di has called strikes at 11 Amazon sites, the most it has ever called out at once, including Leipzig, Dortmund and Koblenz. It accuses Amazon of aggressive workplace monitoring through digital trackers, a claim an Amazon spokesperson in Germany denied.In the US, the Teamsters will rally on Cyber Monday at Amazon's DLX5 facility in Los Angeles and its Goose Island site in Chicago.Unions will mobilise at four Amazon warehouses in Poland. In Luxembourg, a coalition including the OGBL union, Greenpeace and Amnesty International will protest the company's social and environmental record, while Members of the European Parliament will hold a solidarity demonstration in Strasbourg.Across Latin America, workers will mobilise in São Paulo, Brazil, with trade unionists protesting in Bogotá, Colombia, and a solidarity action in Montevideo, Uruguay. Lawmakers in Australia will voice support in Canberra, and further actions are planned in Canada, Japan, the Philippines and South Africa.On November 13, an independent arbitrator set the terms of a three-year agreement for about 800 workers at Amazon's YVR2 fulfilment centre in Delta, represented by Unifor. It raises hourly wages to CAD 29, offers severance of up to 18 weeks and adds a week of vacation for workers with ten years of service.The deal was imposed because Amazon would not reach one at the bargaining table. The province's labour board had earlier found the company ran a long anti-union campaign, including a hiring surge meant to dilute the union vote. Amazon vice-president J. Ofori Agboka called the arbitration "improper [and] unfair" and said the company would go to court if needed."The fact is at Amazon we provide great pay, great benefits and great opportunities, all from day one," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that it employs more than 1.5 million people.Campaigners point out that Amazon made a record $77.7 billion profit in 2025 and plans to spend $220 billion in 2026, much of it on AI and data centres.Workers have notched other gains this year. In July, three Italian transport unions signed national agreements covering all 57 of Amazon's sites in Italy. In April, the US National Labor Relations Board ordered Amazon to bargain with the union at its JFK8 warehouse on Staten Island, an order the company is contesting in court.
Article Summary: Protests stretch from German warehouses to Poland, the US and Brazil. It comes two weeks after warehouse workers in British Columbia, Canada, won the first binding union contract for Amazon employees anywhere in North America. The global days of action run under the Make Amazon Pay banner, convened by UNI Global Union and the Progressive International.

Article Title: North Korea’s answer to ChatGPT has one request for users: Don’t ask about…
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

North Korea’s new chatbot can field questions about game design and headaches. Politics is off limits.The tool, called Fountain of Wisdom, appears to be the country’s first domestically developed AI chatbot, according to 38 North, a US-based research programme that monitors North Korea. It was shown at an IT exhibition in Pyongyang last month and later appeared in a broadcast on the state television channel Ryongnamsan.Martyn Williams, a senior fellow at the Stimson Centre, which runs 38 North, identified Kim Il-sung University’s AI research institute and Pyongyang software developer Phurunhanul Trading as the organisations behind the chatbot.The interface resembles OpenAI’s ChatGPT. The system can answer science and technology questions in Korean or English and translate text, according to the report. Chat histories visible in the broadcast showed someone asking about game-design software. Another query asked what medicine to take for a headache. The footage offered a glimpse of the kinds of everyday questions the chatbot was built to handle.An on-screen notice made the limits clear. “Do not ask questions with sociopolitical content or uncultured questions,” it said, according to Williams’ translation. The notice also told users they would be responsible for any malicious use of the system.The broadcast offered few clues about what powers Fountain of Wisdom. The developers disclosed neither the model nor the hardware it runs on. Williams suggested the team might have used a foreign open-weight model, whose underlying parameters are available for others to download and adapt. The footage did not establish whether that was the case.Williams noted that North Korean hackers and IT workers already appeared to be using foreign AI tools. In August last year, Anthropic said North Korean operatives had used its Claude chatbot to create false professional identities, pass coding tests and complete technical assignments after landing remote jobs at Fortune 500 technology companies.Anthropic said Claude helped some operatives with limited coding skills or English proficiency secure and keep those jobs. The company banned the accounts it linked to the activity and shared its findings with authorities. The 38 North report did not link Fountain of Wisdom to the employment scheme.
Article Summary: The tool, called Fountain of Wisdom, appears to be the country’s first domestically developed AI chatbot. It was shown at an IT exhibition in Pyongyang last month and later appeared in a broadcast on the state television channel Ryongnamsan.

Article Title: Huawei’s Android alternative hits 100 million installs and overtakes iOS in China
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Huawei’s Android-free operating system has crossed 100 million installations. The milestone gives the Chinese tech giant a foothold in mobile software as it looks to take HarmonyOS beyond its home market.Huawei said the figure covers smartphones, tablets and PCs running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7. The company says its ecosystem now offers more than 460,000 apps and services and has over 12 million registered developers, according to a report by South China Morning Post.The strongest gains have come in China. HarmonyOS accounted for 24% of the country’s smartphone operating system market in the second quarter, according to Counterpoint Research. That put Huawei ahead of Apple’s iOS, which had an 18% share, and behind Google’s Android, which led with 58%.The global picture is different. HarmonyOS had a 5% share in the same quarter, while Android accounted for 75% and iOS for 20%. Limited app compatibility remains a hurdle for Huawei overseas, where buyers switching to a HarmonyOS phone may find some of their usual apps unavailable.Richard Yu Chengdong, chairman of Huawei’s consumer business group, called the installation milestone a “landmark moment” in a post on Weibo.In September, he told reporters that Huawei would roll out HarmonyOS internationally in stages over the next one to three years.Huawei first launched HarmonyOS in China in August 2019, months after Washington put the company on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US-origin technology. Early versions could run Android apps. That changed with HarmonyOS 5, also known as HarmonyOS Next, which Huawei introduced in 2024 as a fully self-developed operating system.The shift has coincided with Huawei’s smartphone comeback, helped by the use of its own chips. That recovery has given the company more devices on which to put its software. It has also given developers in China a larger market for apps built specifically for HarmonyOS.The overseas push will test whether Huawei can repeat that cycle in markets where Android and iOS already reach almost every smartphone buyer. A wider selection of local banking, payments and transport apps could give shoppers a reason to switch. Developers, in turn, will need to see enough demand to justify building and maintaining those apps.
Article Summary: HarmonyOS now offers more than 460,000 apps and services and has over 12 million registered developers. The strongest gains have come in China. Limited app compatibility remains a hurdle for Huawei overseas, where buyers switching to a HarmonyOS phone may find their usual apps unavailable.

What Brad Smith said about US taxing companies that have data center overseas

“Well, my sense is that the president is making an important point, but there's some critical nuance we need to think about as well. The point is sort of analogous to the chip industry. I think the administration might want to see the most advanced frontier models trained in the United States, and- and there's room to have that kind of conversation. The nuance is that there's lots of different kinds of data centers. Most data centers actually don't have AI. They're

cloud services

to stream a video, play a video game, run your business, and those have to be located close to customers. They often now have AI because the business applications, even your video games, have an AI element, and the president talked about say, data centers in Finland. You can't support Helsinki from New Jersey any more than you can keep the lights on in Helsinki from an electricity power plant in New Jersey. Those have to be located locally.”

What Donald Trump said about data centres overseas

US President Donald Trump wants American companies to build data centres at home. He has also threatened a tax on those that set them up overseas. Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith pointed to Finland to explain why some facilities need to stay close to customers.Speaking on a recent episode of CBS News’ Face the Nation, Smith said there was room to discuss training the most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models in the US. He said data centres that support services such as video streaming, gaming and business software need to be located near the people and companies that use them.During the CBS interview, Smith said,Speaking at a White House press conference last week, Trump said he wanted US companies to build data centres in the country and threatened penalties for those that build them abroad. He cited concerns about China and drew a parallel with the chip industry, where his administration has pushed for more manufacturing in the US. However, Trump gave no tax rate or timeline during the briefing.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who appeared on the programme before Smith, said he had yet to speak to Trump about the remarks. Bessent said he understood the president’s concern as sensitive technology moving overseas.He said Trump wanted to avoid the kind of dependence on overseas production that had developed in the semiconductor industry.For Microsoft, the scope of any tax would matter. The company has more than 600 data centres across 34 countries. A measure focused on where companies train advanced AI models would affect a narrower set of facilities than a tax covering every new overseas cloud site. As Smith pointed out, a cloud service can also include AI features, so the details would matter for facilities that serve both purposes.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump wants American companies to build data centres at home. He has also threatened a tax on those that set them up overseas. Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith pointed to Finland to explain why some facilities need to stay close to customers.

Article Title: New York mayor Zohran Mamdani blasts Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; reminds him how his 'romantic affairs' may hurt Americans; says: Working people in the US didn't sign up for their pensions being tied to
Article Text:
The $81 billion remark made by Zohran Mamdani

Concerns over wealth concentration

AI stocks and market dependence

Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The investigation into Jensen Huang will still run its course

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has criticised the outsized influence of major technology companies on financial markets, using the recent controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as an example of how the personal affairs of powerful executives can affect ordinary Americans. According to a report by Politico, speaking to reporters at a recent press conference, Mamdani said that he was concerned that the financial security of working people could be affected by the developments surrounding one of the technology industry’s most influential leaders. He also emphasised that the workers should not have their retirement savings and pension funds exposed to volatility linked to the personal conduct of corporate executives.“I do not think that working people across the country signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Jensen Huang's fidelity to his marriage. And yet for many days that had a massive impact,” Mamdani said.Mamdani also noted a rumoured divorce settlement of about $81 billion, which he said would cover a year of universal child care for every 3- and 4-year-old in the United States. There has been no announcement of a divorce between Huang and his wife.The $81 billion figure is a rumor Mamdani cited, not a confirmed number.Mamdani also talked about the reports and rumours regarding the personal life of Jensen Huang and the potential financial implications that had been discussed in public. Referring to a widely reported estimate of a possible divorce settlement, Mamdani noted that the figure being discussed was approximately $81 billion.According to Mamdani, such a large sum highlights the scale of wealth concentrated in the hands of a small number of individuals. He compared the reported figure with the potential cost of funding universal childcare across the United States for three- and four-year-old children for a year.The mayor then invoked a famous quote from former US Supreme Court Justice Louis Brandeis, saying, “We can have democracy, we can have great wealth concentrated in the hands of a few. We cannot have both.”The criticism made by Mamdani goes beyond Huang and Nvidia. He also warned about the excessive reliance on stocks related to artificial intelligence with the broader US economy. He further stressed that dominance of AI companies in public markets raises questions about economic resilience and concentration of power.“When you look at our stock market, and you look at how disproportionately dependent it is on artificial intelligence-related stocks, it cannot help but give you a sense of concern about just how much this technology is now dominant,” he said.Jensen Huang is back in charge at Nvidia, less than two weeks after he quit the company he co-founded. The chipmaker's board has voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately. The board said a series of meetings with Huang left it satisfied with his candour and his ability to lead. It added that input from senior levels of the US government gave it confidence his return poses no national security risk. The move is a complete U-turn from last week, when the same board said it had no plans to bring him back.Huang resigned on November 12, ending a 33-year run as CEO. His exit came days after Nvidia said it would investigate reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Those reports linked him to a woman US officials believe was recruited by China's spy agency. CFO Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO.Huang's return does not end the probe. A committee made up only of independent directors, working with independent counsel, is looking into the foreign intelligence reports. The board said the investigation will proceed to its conclusion. Huang has said he fully supports it and will cooperate.Nvidia is also adding new layers of oversight. The board recently set up a National Security and Export Control Committee, again made up only of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. It is bringing in counsel with national security experience, who will hire specialist advisers of their own. The company has also started a search for a new Chief Compliance Officer, who will report to the board's Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with ongoing government investigations. Huang and general counsel Tim Teter are scheduled to answer questions from US House committees behind closed doors on December 1 and 2.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has criticised the outsized influence of major technology companies on financial markets. He used the recent controversy involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as an example of how the personal affairs of powerful executives can affect ordinary Americans. He also stressed that dominance of AI companies in public markets raises questions about economic resilience and concentration of power.

Article Title: Australia passes law that may result in massive fines for Google, Meta and other internet platforms if…
Article Text:
Australia’s another ‘regulatory blow’ to US-based tech giants

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Free speech, privacy and over-censorship concerns

Australia has passed a sweeping new online safety law requiring major internet platforms, including Google and Meta, to proactively eliminate harmful content and features, or risk penalties of up to 5% of their global revenue. The legislation, known as the Digital Duty of Care, will take effect in one year. Replacing an existing patchwork of separate online codes of conduct with a single, all-encompassing law, the rules shift the responsibility directly onto tech companies to prioritise the safety of Australian users. Under the new law, platforms that breach the rules face fines of up to 5% of their global turnover or A$109 million ($72 million), whichever is greater – a steep financial threat for tech giants that generate hundreds of billions of dollars in annual revenue, news agency Reuters reported.“The Digital Duty of Care is a landmark safety reform in the vein of compulsory seatbelts, plain packaging for cigarettes and gun reform. Big Tech can no longer be under any illusions – they are responsible for keeping Australians safe on their platforms, and we will hold them to account if they fail to do so,” Communications Minister Anika Wells said in a statement following the law's passage.The Digital Duty of Care adds to a string of moves by Australia against the largely US-based internet industry, which the government has accused of undermining its right to regulate digital products used within its borders.In December 2025, Australia became the first country in the world to ban children under 16 from using social media. Moreover, the Australian government also plans to force major internet platforms to pay licensing fees for news content to reimburse news media organisations.While technology companies have broadly supported the government's goal of protecting children and curbing online harm, most opposed the legislation, arguing that it gives government officials too much discretion to decide what qualifies as harmful content. As per the report, industry groups have also cautioned that the threat of severe fines could push platforms to become overly heavy-handed with takedowns simply to avoid punishment.Specifically, the law prohibits material that “encourages or promotes hostile attitudes towards women or gender equality” as well as content that “glorifies crime or encourages dangerous stunts or seriously harmful practices” – broad classifications that free speech advocates warn are open to wide interpretation, the report noted.
Article Summary: Australia has passed a sweeping new online safety law requiring major internet platforms to proactively eliminate harmful content. The legislation, known as the Digital Duty of Care, will take effect in one year. Under the new law, platforms that breach the rules face fines of up to 5% of their global turnover or A$109 million ($72 million), whichever is greater.

Article Title: Nykaa brings honey-powered beauty brand Gisou to India
Article Text:
Nykaa expands premium global beauty portfolio

A beauty brand built on six generations of beekeeping

Bestselling haircare and lip products arrive in India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Expanding demand for premium haircare

Beauty and lifestyle retailer Nykaa has announced the launch of Dutch beauty brand Gisou in India through an exclusive partnership, bringing the globally recognised honey-powered haircare, beauty and fragrance label founded by Negin Mirsalehi to Indian consumers.The brand will be available exclusively through Nykaa’s online platform and selected retail stores across the country. As Gisou’s exclusive importer and retail partner in India, Nykaa said it will introduce the brand’s signature "Honey Glow" beauty rituals and a range of its bestselling products.The launch marks another addition to Nykaa's growing portfolio of premium international beauty brands. The company said its Global Store platform is designed to help international brands enter and scale within the Indian beauty market through its import, distribution and retail capabilities.Commenting on the partnership, Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said Gisou has emerged as one of the most distinctive brands in the beauty and haircare space by combining heritage with a modern approach to beauty.“Gisou is one of the most distinctive and innovative brands in haircare and in beauty today, bringing together a unique heritage and a modern approach to beauty that resonates with consumers around the world,” Nayar said, adding that Nykaa is pleased to introduce the brand to Indian customers.Founded in 2015 by Negin Mirsalehi, Gisou traces its roots to six generations of family beekeeping heritage in the Netherlands. The brand's products are centred around proprietary Mirsalehi Honey, sourced from the family's bee garden and positioned as a key ingredient across its beauty portfolio.Mirsalehi said the launch represents an important milestone for the brand.“We’re so excited to bring Gisou to India with Nykaa. What began in my family’s Bee Garden with a homemade honey-infused hair oil has grown into a global beauty brand and bringing that story to India is a very special moment for me,” she said.Indian consumers will gain access to several of Gisou’s flagship products, including the Honey Infused Hair Oil, Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Hair Mask, Honey Milk Active Repair Leave-In Conditioner, and the brand’s popular Honey Infused Lip Oils range.The Honey Infused Hair Oil, which was Gisou’s first product, is designed to provide hydration, shine, heat protection and frizz control using a blend of Mirsalehi Honey and botanical oils. The Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Hair Mask combines honey, ceramides and hyaluronic acid to target hydration and hair strength.Meanwhile, the Honey Milk Active Repair Leave-In Conditioner is positioned as a lightweight repair treatment featuring honey, milk proteins and ceramides. The company says the product helps detangle hair while offering heat protection and reducing frizz.The launch comes as India's premium beauty and haircare market continues to attract global brands looking to tap into increasing consumer interest in specialised hair treatments, ingredient-led products and luxury beauty offerings.With Gisou's arrival, Nykaa is strengthening its position as a destination for international premium beauty brands while giving Indian consumers access to a label that has built a strong following globally through its honey-based formulations and social-media-driven brand presence.
Article Summary: Nykaa has announced the launch of Dutch beauty brand Gisou in India through an exclusive partnership. The brand will be available exclusively through Nykaa’s online platform and selected retail stores across the country. Founded in 2015 by Negin Mirsalehi, the brand traces its roots to six generations of family beekeeping heritage in the Netherlands.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg lets Meta's Muse AI monitor Thanksgiving turkey while he plays video games
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and wife Priscilla Chan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta's Muse AI crosses 10 million downloads

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg found an unusual way to use AI this Thanksgiving. The tech billionaire used the company's Muse AI agent to monitor his turkey-smoking process while he played video games, claiming the AI-assisted effort helped him win his family's annual turkey-smoking competition. Mark Zuckerberg shared a video on Facebook showing Muse tracking the cooking progress. In the video, his wife, Priscilla Chan, can be heard asking, “Mark, you are supposed to be making the turkey. People are going to be here soon. What are you doing?”Instead of leaving his game, Zuckerberg asked Muse for an update on the turkey.“We’re on it. Turkey two is still tracking. Breast was climbing steadily and the pit is holding near your target, so that pull around four should still get you set for guests,” the AI agent replied.Zuckerberg responded, “Awesome.”He later shared a picture of the finished turkey on his Facebook Story with the caption, “Winning Turkey smoked by Muse.” He also joked that Chan had conceded their annual competition after seeing the results and asked Muse to prepare her turkey as well.The Thanksgiving demonstration comes as Meta's Muse AI gains popularity among users in the US. Article Title: US government allows the country's largest telecom company to discontinue copper landline service in Arizona, Delaware, New Jersey, Ohio and five other states: Why this has made some consumers upset
Article Text:
Why Verizon wants to retire copper lines

Why some consumers are upset

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FCC cites Verizon commitments

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved a request from Verizon, the country’s largest telecom carrier, to discontinue its legacy copper-based landline telephone service in nine states, a move that has drawn criticism from some customers who fear losing a reliable means of communication during emergencies. According to a report by PCMag, the decisions will enable Verizon to retire traditional copper landline networks serving residential and business customers in Arizona, Delaware, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Utah and Virginia. The approval comes after the FCC paused the proposal for nearly two months to review concerns raised by hundreds of residents and local communities.In its ruling, FCC has said that Verizon had met the agency’s requirements for technology-transition service discontinuances and found no evidence that ending the copper services would negatively affect the public interest. The commission also noted Verizon's commitment to continue providing copper-based telephone service in locations where reliable alternatives are not available.Verizon has been looking to replace its decades-old copper network with fiber and wireless-based services, arguing that the infrastructure is expensive to maintain and its also vulnerable to theft and damage. The carrier further added that the present copper lines are also not equipped to meet the demands of modern connectivity.As per the company, only a small percentage of customers continue to rely on legacy voice services delivered through copper networks.Along with this, Verizon also informed the regulators that alternative options, include fibre-based phone services and wireless offerings, are available in many of the affected areas. The FCC said Verizon had confirmed the availability of one or more adequate replacement services for impacted customers.The approval follows a pause. In late September, the FCC said it needed more time to review the plan after receiving hundreds of comments and concerns from consumers and a US lawmaker. Notices already sent to landline customers added to unease. The pause was not a denial, and the FCC described it as not a final determination on the merits.The reasons for concern are practical. Copper phones work with simple equipment and, for many people, have long been seen as a dependable backup. Devices such as fire alarm panels, elevator emergency phones and fax machines run on this analog service. Customers worry about whether a replacement will work as reliably, which is why Verizon's promise to keep service where no good alternative exists matters.The report also added that FCC revealed that Verizon has already contacted the customers who had concerns and also said that many of the users will not get affected by the discontinuance. As per the commission, the company has also informed the users about their present copper-based Plain Old Telephone Service (POTS) will continue and the plans to follow up with automated notifications where permitted. The regulator also added that Verizon has been working to address the concerns of the local government in the affected areas for the clearance and approval.
Article Summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved a request from Verizon to discontinue its legacy copper-based landline telephone service in nine states. The move has drawn criticism from some customers who fear losing a reliable means of communication during emergencies. The approval comes after the FCC paused the proposal for nearly two months to review concerns raised by hundreds of residents.

Instamart adds private labels as competition heats up

Swiggy’s quick commerce unit Instamart is reportedly cutting 340 jobs. A report by The Economic Times cited people familiar with the matter, who said the latest round of job cuts comes as part of a restructuring exercise. The cuts mark the first major development at Instamart under CEO Nandita Sinha and come as the company faces growing competition from Blinkit and Amazon Now.Sinha, the former CEO of fashion e-commerce platform Myntra , took charge of Instamart on August 3, succeeding Amitesh Jha. The restructuring comes as Instamart’s losses have widened. The quick commerce unit reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 895 crore in the September quarter, up from Rs 778 crore in the previous quarter. That translates to a sequential increase of Rs 117 crore, or about 15%. Swiggy said it believed Instamart’s losses had peaked. At the group level, Swiggy’s consolidated net loss narrowed to Rs 922 crore in the September quarter from Rs 1,092 crore in the same period a year earlier.The layoffs come even as Instamart steps up investment in its quick commerce business. The company recently launched two private labels: Noice for snacks and beverages, and Nectr for fresh fruits and vegetables. The launches give Instamart its own brands in two grocery categories as it competes with Blinkit and Amazon Now.Swiggy has also outlined a change to how it handles inventory. In its letter to shareholders accompanying the September quarter results, the company said it would begin moving to an inventory-led business model from the middle of the third quarter of FY27. Swiggy expects the process to take two to three quarters.The move follows Swiggy’s transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company in August, the same month Sinha took charge of Instamart. Under an inventory-led model, the platform takes ownership of the goods it sells, giving it more direct control over what it stocks. Swiggy set out the timeline for the shift in its shareholder letter. The report did not specify which teams were affected by the layoffs or whether the cuts were linked to the planned inventory transition.

Germany employment protections may shape plans

Europe’s largest software company SAP SE, is reportedly preparing to cut at least 10,000 positions as part of a sweeping restructuring which is aimed at transforming its business for the artificial intelligence era, as reported by Bloomberg. The planned layoffs are said to affect at least 9% of the company’s global workforce, however, the final number of job cuts have not been determined and the report adds that the final number could change after the discussions with the labour representatives. Presently, SAP employs more than 110,000 people across the world.The planned job cuts at SAP comes as its chief executive officer Christian Klein accelerated the process to reposition the German software giant around artificial intelligence. As per the Bloomberg report, SAP has also reorganised its executive board twice this year as part of the strategy with two of its six board members set to levee the Walldorf-based company in March.The report further states that leadership at SAP is also redesigning the way the company develops and sells software products, with a strong focus on embedding AI capabilities across its application portfolio. This move follows the earlier attempt of SAP to roll out AI-powered products which reportedly faced challenges."SAP continuously reviews its organisation to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs," the company said in a statement to Bloomberg, declining to comment on whether job reductions are being planned.As per the report, as part of the ongoing restructuring exercise all the business units have been asked to identify the areas where the company can reduce costs. It is said that the product, engineering teams, along with sales departments, are expected to face particular scrutiny.The changes also coincide with leadership shifts within the company. Klein has assumed most of the responsibilities previously overseen by product chief Muhammad Alam, whose contract expires in March and was not renewed. Meanwhile, sales chief Thomas Saueressig recently announced plans to leave SAP to become CEO of internet services provider Ionos Group SE.The upcoming job cuts at SAP comes less than three years after the European technology giant initiated a major restructuring programme. In 2024, the company fired around 10,000 employees as part of an effort to reduce cost. That restructuring was mainly carried out via voluntary departures and employee retraining programmes, enabling SAP to keep its overall workforce relatively stable by hiring new roles. The company ultimately maintained broadly flat headcount levels despite the reductions.Any fresh round of job cuts is said to face scrutiny in Germany, where SAP employs a significant portion of its staff. Earlier this tear, the labour council of the company negotiated an employment guarantee which runs till 2028. Still, signs of a hiring slowdown have already emerged. Speaking at a Morgan Stanley conference last week, SAP Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam said the company's workforce had grown slightly during the year but suggested that trend may not continue."Our headcount has increased a little bit over the course of the year," Asam said, adding that he "would be really surprised" if that trend did not reverse.
Article Summary: SAP is reportedly preparing to cut at least 10,000 positions as part of a sweeping restructuring. The planned layoffs are said to affect at least 9% of the company’s global workforce. SAP employs more than 110,000 people across the world.

World football’s governing body, FIFA, confirmed on Thursday (November 26) that it has been hit by a criminal cyberattack in which hackers gained unauthorised access to and stole a “limited set of personal and business information. ” The Switzerland-based organisation stated that it is working closely with relevant authorities, including law enforcement, following the breach.“FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data. Article Title: Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze gets judge's approval; made Google founder Sergey Brin exit New York real estate fund; 'sold for just 6 cents on...'
Article Text:
Judge says Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze has a “rational basis”

Zohran Mamdani calls ruling a victory for tenants

Judge criticises campaign pledge but upholds policy

Sergey Brin’s exit renewed focus on investor concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A New York City judge has upheld Mayor Zohran Mamdani ’s controversial rent freeze for roughly one million rent-stabilised, handing an important political victory to the Democratic socialist mayor whose affordability-focused housing agenda has drawn both praise from tenants and fierce opposition from landlords. As reported by The Guardian, Manhattan Supreme Court issued an order on November 25, in which Judge Brendan Lantry dismissed the lawsuit filed by a coalition of the landlord who were looking to block the rent freeze policy of Mamdani. The measure freezes rents on one-and two-year leases for rent-stabilised apartments beginning on or after October 1. This ruling from the court comes months after the policy attracted the attention from investors in New York’s multifamily housing sector, including Google co-founder Sergey Brin , whose exit from a New York real estate find at a steep loss had previously been linked to growing concerns over the future of rent-stabilised housing investments.The legal challenge was launched after New York City’s Rent Guidelines Board approved the rent freeze in June. Landlords argued that the board had relied on a flawed process and ignored evidence showing rising operating costs, including insurance, maintenance and taxes.However, Judge Lantry said the court’s role was not to determine whether the policy was wise or whether it could negatively affect the broader real estate market.Instead, the court had to decide whether the board’s decision was arbitrary, unreasonable or lacked a rational basis.The judge ultimately concluded that the landlords had “failed to establish” that the board acted in an unreasonable or arbitrary manner. As a result, the court upheld the rent freeze as valid.Reacting to the court order, Mayor Mamdani described the ruling as a win for the New Yorkers who are struggling with the high cost of living of the city. “This is a victory for tenants, for affordability and for the principle that working New Yorkers deserve a city they can afford to live in,” Mamdani said in a statement reported by The New York Times. “Because housing is not a luxury. It is a basic necessity.”For those unaware, rent freeze was one of the important promises Mamdani made in his mayoral campaign. The policy majorly focuses on addressing the housing affordability in a city where millions of people are facing the increasing living costs.Despite ruling in favour of the freeze, Judge Lantry was critical of Mamdani’s campaign slogan to “freeze the rent”. The judge described the promise as “reckless and irresponsible”, noting that New York City mayors do not have unilateral authority to set rents on stabilised units. That responsibility belongs to the Rent Guidelines Board. Nevertheless, he found that the board, which approved the measure, acted within its authority and that its decision should stand.The court victory also revives attention on the broader impact of rent regulations on investment in New York housing. Earlier report by Bloomberg revealed that Google co-founder Sergey Brin quietly walked away from a sizeable bet on New York City apartments, selling his stake in a struggling real estate fund for just six cents on the dollar. One of the world's richest man offloaded his holding back to the fund's manager, A&E Real Estate.Amphitheatre LLC, an entity tied to Brin, sold its shares in a fund holding nearly 5,900 units across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx. Many of those apartments fall under New York's rent-stabilization program. A&E confirmed the buyout without naming Brin, saying the investor "was willing to accept six cents on the dollar on their original equity investment to divest itself from the New York City multifamily sector. "
Article Summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s controversial rent freeze for roughly one million rent- stabilised apartments has been upheld by a New York City judge. Judge Brendan Lantry dismissed the lawsuit filed by a coalition of the landlord who were looking to block the rent freeze policy. Judge Lantry said the court had to decide whether the Rent Guidelines Board's decision was arbitrary, unreasonable or lacked a rational basis. The judge described the promise as “reckless and irresponsible”

When Nvidia’s board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO this week, shareholders were not the only ones celebrating a windfall. The Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation, which is a private charity run by Huang’s wife, Lori, saw the value of its massive Nvidia stock holdings jump by roughly $2.3 billion in a single day. Citing Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement, Fortune reported that the foundation holds approximately 59 million Nvidia shares. As Nvidia’s stock surged more than 30% on Monday to close at $165.05, the value of the foundation’s stake climbed to roughly $9.7 billion – up $2.3 billion from Friday’s (November 20) closing price.Lori Huang has served as president of the foundation since 2014, while Jensen serves as secretary and chief financial officer (CFO). She is also co-trustee of the family trusts holding the majority of the couple’s Nvidia shares, which make up the bulk of a personal fortune valued by Forbes at roughly $144 billion.While the Huangs maintain a quiet organisational footprint, their public philanthropic commitments have steadily grown in recent years.In July, the foundation donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to fund a new art, architecture, and design college in San Francisco.Last November, it committed $5 million annually to the San Francisco Opera. In 2025, the couple gave $22.5 million to the California College of the Arts, and in 2022, they donated $50 million to Oregon State University.Huang has previously framed these gifts as forward-looking investments rather than simple charity. “I don’t give anything away. Hilton Foundation.Notably, the charity has no website and, despite its size, reported no paid staff as of 2023. The Huangs continue to transfer shares into the fund; in June 2025, their living trust donated 440,000 Nvidia shares (worth around $60 million) to the foundation, according to an SEC filing cited by CNBC.

Article Title: US government considered using a 76-year-old Cold War law in a way never tried before to bring back Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
Article Text:
Jensen Huang gestures as employees applaud his return to office after NVIDIA reinstated him as the company's CEO, in Santa Clara, California, US (Reuters)

The Defense Production Act has never been used to put someone in charge of a company

The idea of using a wartime law for Jensen Huang started in Silicon Valley

Jensen Huang says Trump did not pressure Nvidia's board

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Senior Pentagon officials discussed invoking the Defense Production Act (DPA), a 1950 wartime law, to pressure Nvidia's board into reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, The Washington Post reported. The talks took place over the weekend, before Nvidia announced Huang's return on Monday, according to three people familiar with the debate. The Pentagon has denied that they happened.Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his deputy Steve Feinberg reportedly discussed using the law as leverage, arguing that Nvidia was critical to US national security. Emil Michael, the Pentagon's chief technology officer and a former Uber executive, was also part of the conversations.The DPA offers no clear route to installing a CEO, but it could have worked as a warning. One Trump administration official told the Post the government could use it to force Nvidia to shift more of its production to military projects. That could have dented the chipmaker's plans and profits.It is unclear what, if anything, reached Nvidia, or whether the idea made it to President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance.A person familiar with the board's thinking said directors did not see the government's arguments as a threat."The conversations described between DOW senior leaders never happened and no such proposal was made by the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or Under Secretary," a Pentagon official said. DOW refers to the Department of War, the administration's preferred name for the Defense Department. Nvidia declined to comment.Congress passed the DPA a few months into the Korean War. It lets the president push private companies to put military and emergency needs first. The first Trump administration used it to get General Motors making ventilators during the Covid-19 pandemic. It has never been used to install a leader at a private company.Bill Greenwalt, a DPA expert at the American Enterprise Institute, said the law essentially puts government orders ahead of everyone else's. Nothing in it supports tying Nvidia up in contracts, he said, and export controls would have been a more effective lever.Pete Harrell, a visiting scholar at Georgetown, said the administration seems "interested in getting five companies in a room and kind of telling them what to do."The pitch had been doing the rounds in tech circles for days. Last week, investor Balaji Srinivasan posted that the Department of War could step in on Huang's side, calling it a "Defense Production Act, but for the restoration of Jensen Huang."A private push ran alongside it. The Financial Times reported that Huang's friends, including Travis Kalanick, Brad Gerstner and Marc Andreessen, set up a "war room" to lobby the board and eventually pulled in Trump and Vance.Huang resigned on November 12 after admitting to affairs. One was with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who US officials believe passed information to Chinese intelligence. Eleven days later, the board voted unanimously to bring him back. Nvidia shares jumped more than 30%, the biggest one-day gain in market value on record for a US company, according to The Wall Street Journal.Trump and Vance spent the weekend passing assurances on to directors, the Journal reported. These included Attorney General Todd Blanche's word that Huang was not the target of any Justice Department probe. Semafor reported that Trump backed Huang's return because Huang supports US open-weight AI models.Huang, however, told employees at an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that claims of Trump pressuring the board were "completely untrue," The New York Times reported.He is due before the House Foreign Affairs Committee next Tuesday and the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday. The Commerce Department blacklisted Megaspeed on Monday, and Nvidia has said it will hire a chief compliance officer.
Article Summary: Pentagon officials discussed invoking the Defense Production Act (DPA), a 1950 wartime law, to pressure Nvidia's board into reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. The talks took place over the weekend, before Nvidia announced Huang's return on Monday. The Pentagon has denied that they happened.

Article Title: Samsung Display partners with ams OSRAM for microLED technology
Article Text:
Samsung Display partners with ams OSRAM for microLED technology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Samsung Display has signed an investment agreement to acquire a 9.1% equity interest in ams OSRAM for approximately EUR 210 million ($230.39 million). Under the agreement, Samsung Display will acquire 9,984,439 newly issued shares of ams OSRAM and is expected to become its largest shareholder upon closing. Separately, the two companies have also entered into a strategic partnership to jointly develop next-generation ultra-small microLED technology for display applications. Through this collaboration, Samsung Display plans to step up research and development to accelerate the potential commercialization of ultra-small microLED technology, including efforts to improve its efficiency and cost competitiveness.With more than 120 years of history, ams OSRAM has extensive technological expertise in advanced epitaxy, LED miniaturization and high-volume LED manufacturing, as well as high-density integration. Through its investment in ams OSRAM, Samsung Display plans to extend its world-leading technological expertise in OLED to inorganic self-emissive technologies. In particular, the company plans to evaluate the performance and applicability of ultra-small LEDs manufactured by ams OSRAM and establish the manufacturing processes and production technologies needed to commercialize next-generation ultra-small microLED displays.The company will also explore mid- to long-term business opportunities across a wide range of applications, from ultra-small to ultra-large displays.Samsung Display expects to complete the share acquisition in early 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including applicable regulatory approvals.“This partnership marks a major strategic milestone for ams OSRAM. It creates a funded pathway for a novel next-generation ultra-small microLED technology from technology development towards potential industrialization, while Samsung Display’s strategic investment in ams OSRAM underscores our shared commitment to its successful development and commercialization,” said Aldo Kamper, CEO of ams OSRAM.“Ultra-small microLED is a next-generation inorganic self-emissive technology with the potential to overcome the limitations of existing technologies in areas such as brightness and lifetime. Its potential is not limited to any particular product category, but extends across an exceptionally broad range of applications, from ultra-small to ultra-large displays,” said Chung Yi, President and CEO of Samsung Display.“This investment reflects our determination not to remain complacent with where we are today, but to proactively respond to technological evolution and emerging market demand while securing new engines for future growth,” Yi added.
Article Summary: Samsung Display has signed an investment agreement to acquire a 9.1% equity interest in ams OSRAM for approximately EUR 210 million ($230.39 million) The two companies have also entered into a strategic partnership to jointly develop next-generation ultra-small microLED technology for display applications.

Article Title: CEO of Europe's biggest tech company ASML, warns US against cutting off chip supplies to China: You don't completely frustrate a country and invite that country to...
Article Text:
ASML CEO warns US on China curbs

ASML CEO says older machines keep China tied to Western tech

Washington's chip rules have tightened fast this month

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New US export control bills could reach ASML's machines next

ASML chief executive Christophe Fouquet has warned the US against cutting China off from Western chip technology completely, saying harsher export controls could push Beijing to speed up work on its own alternatives. Speaking on Semafor's Future Proof, Fouquet said controls are necessary but work only up to a point. "You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don't completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development," he said.ASML is the only company in the world that makes the lithography machines needed to produce the most advanced AI chips. Valued at around $520 billion, the Dutch firm sits right at the centre of the US-China tech fight.Fouquet's case rests on what he calls a "generation gap". The equipment ASML ships to China today is more than a decade behind its most advanced tools. Selling those older machines, he argued, keeps Chinese chipmakers on Western hardware instead of racing to replace it.He pointed to ASML's long run in the country. "For almost 30 years, we have been able to keep an extremely high market share in China, very high means close to 100%, which means that they have accepted to rely on our technology with the idea that they had access to it," Fouquet said.Fouquet's warning arrives as the US moves in the opposite direction, and much of that push traces back to Nvidia. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12 after reports of an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed. US intelligence officials believe she was in touch with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during the relationship. Beijing has denied spying.Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on November 23 after pressure from President Donald Trump. US officials told congressional staffers this week there were no signs Alice Huang passed on intelligence of significance, but the policy fallout has not slowed.Megaspeed, under Justice Department investigation over alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China, has been added to the Commerce Department's entity list. The department has also moved to require licences for AI chips headed to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia that supply significant computing power to Chinese firms. Nvidia has since paused some sales of its top chips in those four countries.Three bills are gaining ground in Congress as well. The Chip Security Act would require location checks on advanced AI chips after they ship. The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress oversight of chip export licences to countries of concern. The MATCH Act, which targets loopholes around chipmaking equipment and export rules in allied countries, is the one that reaches ASML directly.That has drawn pushback from the Netherlands. Dutch lawmakers have pressed their government to resist US legislation that would further restrict chipmaking equipment exports to China, Semafor reported. ASML alone accounts for about 2.2% of Dutch GDP, and the country has already agreed, under US pressure, to stop shipping ASML's most advanced machines to China.Lawmakers could add the bills to the annual defence policy bill expected next month. Huang is scheduled to appear before three House committees next week, followed by a public Senate Banking Committee hearing on December 3.
Article Summary: ASML CEO says older machines keep China tied to Western tech. ASML is the only company in the world that makes the lithography machines needed to produce the most advanced AI chips. Dutch lawmakers have pressed their government to resist US legislation that would further restrict chipmaking equipment exports to China.

Article Title: Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses may be banned in the Netherlands; lawyer tells court: Each invasion of privacy is worse than...
